name: OCO-2 Level 2 Bias-corrected XCO2 (Lite)
summary: Column-averaged dry-air CO2 (XCO2) from NASA's Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2, with high precision and fine footprints.
spatial: 1.29 km x 2.25 km footprints, ~10 km swath
coverage: Global land and ocean (glint); sun-lit only
strengths: Fine footprint good for point sources and urban plumes
limitations: No data under cloud, aerosol or at night
Sparse at high latitudes in winter
bestFor: Regional to global CO2 inversions, urban/plume studies, validation of models.
useWith: Pair with OCO-3 for longer record; compare with GOSAT for bias checks; use CAMS or CarbonTracker as a model reference.
citation: OCO-2 Science Team et al., OCO-2 Level 2 bias-corrected XCO2 and other select fields from the full-physics retrieval aggregated as daily files, NASA GES DISC.

name: OCO-3 Level 2 Bias-corrected XCO2 (Lite)
summary: XCO2 and SIF from the OCO-3 instrument on the ISS, including Snapshot Area Maps over cities and emission hotspots.
temporal: Irregular; ISS orbit samples all local times
strengths: SAM mode maps cities and power plants in a ~80 x 80 km block
bestFor: City- and facility-scale CO2 studies, diurnal-cycle analysis.
useWith: Combine with OCO-2 to extend density; keep time-of-day differences in mind.
citation: OCO-3 Science Team et al., OCO-3 Level 2 bias-corrected XCO2 and other select fields from the full-physics retrieval aggregated as daily files, NASA GES DISC.

name: GOSAT TANSO-FTS XCO2 (ACOS) and XCH4 (NIES)
summary: The longest satellite record of both XCO2 and XCH4, from Japan's Greenhouse gases Observing SATellite.
spatial: ~10.5 km diameter footprints, spaced ~250 km apart
access: Free; Earthdata Login for ACOS XCO2. XCH4 and NIES versions need separate registration at the NIES GOSAT archive (currently under maintenance).
strengths: Multiple independent retrievals allow uncertainty comparison
bestFor: Long-term trends, regional flux inversions, CO2 and CH4 together.
useWith: Use as the long baseline and OCO-2/3 for dense recent data; use TROPOMI for dense CH4.
citation: NIES GOSAT Project, GOSAT TANSO-FTS Level 2 data products (see GOSAT Data Archive Service for version-specific citation).

name: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI Methane (XCH4)
summary: Daily global methane columns at high resolution, widely used to find large methane emitters.
spatial: 5.5 km x 7 km (7 km x 7 km before Aug 2019)
strengths: Detects super-emitters (oil and gas, coal, landfills)
limitations: Gaps over cloud, snow and dark ocean
Retrieval biases over bright and complex surfaces
bestFor: Methane hotspot detection, regional emission estimates.
useWith: Pair with GOSAT for CH4 baseline and EDGAR for inventory comparison.
citation: Copernicus Sentinel-5P (processed by ESA), TROPOMI Level 2 Methane Total Column. Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem.

name: NOAA CarbonTracker CT2026
summary: Data-assimilation system that estimates surface CO2 fluxes and 3D CO2 mole fractions from atmospheric observations.
spatial: 3° x 2° global, nested 1° x 1° over North America
limitations: Results depend on prior fluxes and transport
bestFor: Context fields for satellite data, flux budgets, boundary conditions.
useWith: Compare with CAMS to see model spread; use alongside OCO-2 as an independent check.
citation: Jacobson, A. R. et al., CarbonTracker CT2026, NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory.

name: CAMS Global Inversion-optimised GHG Fluxes and Concentrations
summary: Copernicus atmospheric inversions that assimilate surface and satellite data to estimate fluxes and concentrations.
limitations: Product version changes can affect time series
bestFor: Long-term budgets, multi-gas studies, model comparison.
useWith: Use with CarbonTracker for ensemble spread.
citation: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), CAMS global inversion-optimised greenhouse gas fluxes and concentrations. ECMWF ADS.

name: MiCASA Land Carbon Flux
summary: NASA's satellite-driven land carbon model estimating NPP, heterotrophic respiration, and fire emissions for use as prior fluxes in inversions.
limitations: Bottom-up model, not optimized to CO2 observations
bestFor: Land biosphere priors and bottom-up flux comparison.
useWith: Combine with ODIAC (fossil) and an ocean product to build a full flux prior.
citation: Weir, B. et al., MiCASA Land Carbon Flux, NASA GES DISC (verify version-specific citation).

name: ODIAC Fossil Fuel CO2 Emission Dataset
summary: High-resolution gridded global fossil fuel CO2 emissions using national totals and satellite nightlights plus point source data.
variables: Fossil fuel CO2 emissions (tonne C per cell)
strengths: Widely used as prior in urban CO2 inversions
limitations: Spatial distribution partly based on nightlights
useWith: Compare with EDGAR and Vulcan; combine with OCO-2/3 for urban analysis.
citation: Oda, T. and Maksyutov, S., ODIAC Fossil Fuel CO2 Emissions Dataset, NIES (cite version used).

name: EDGAR Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research
summary: Bottom-up emissions by country, sector and grid cell for greenhouse gases and air pollutants.
variables: Emissions by sector (power, industry, transport, buildings, agriculture, waste)
limitations: Uncertainty larger for CH4 and for developing countries
bestFor: Sector-level emission analysis, comparison to top-down estimates.
useWith: Compare to TROPOMI-derived CH4 emissions and to ODIAC for CO2.
citation: Crippa, M. et al., EDGAR (Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research), European Commission JRC (cite release used).

name: Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED5 and GFED4s)
summary: Burned area and fire emissions of carbon and trace gases, including small-fire detection.
variables: CO2 / CH4 / CO emissions by vegetation type
temporal: Monthly (with daily and 3-hourly fractions in beta)
access: Free; SFTP credentials are posted on the data page
limitations: Coarse grid for local fire work
bestFor: Fire contribution to carbon budgets and atmospheric inversions.
useWith: Combine with MiCASA, ODIAC, and an ocean flux dataset.
citation: Chen, Y. et al., GFED5 burned area and fire emissions, Earth System Science Data, 2023; van der Werf, G. R. et al., GFED4s, Earth System Science Data, 2017.

name: Vulcan V4 Fossil Fuel CO2 Emissions (US)
summary: Facility- and road-level fossil fuel CO2 emissions for the contiguous United States. Version 4 is annual; version 3 offers hourly fields for 2010-2015.
variables: Fossil CO2 emissions by sector (onroad, electricity, commercial, residential, etc.)
strengths: Built from bottom-up facility and traffic data
limitations: Period covered ends earlier than satellites
bestFor: US urban CO2 and diurnal emission studies.
useWith: Validate against ODIAC and EDGAR; pair with OCO-3 SAMs over US cities.
citation: Gurney, K. R. et al., Vulcan: High-Resolution Annual Fossil Fuel CO2 Emissions in USA, 2010-2022, Version 4, ORNL DAAC.

name: Global Carbon Budget
summary: Annual synthesis of the global CO2 budget: fossil emissions, land-use change, atmospheric growth, ocean and land sinks.
spatial: Global and national totals; gridded versions available
useWith: Use to sanity check sums of ODIAC/EDGAR + MiCASA + GFED fluxes.
citation: Friedlingstein, P. et al., Global Carbon Budget 2025, Earth System Science Data.

name: Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON)
summary: Ground-based solar-viewing FTIR spectrometers giving the accuracy standard used to validate satellite XCO2 and XCH4.
limitations: Site records start and end at different dates
useWith: Compare with OCO-2/3, GOSAT and TROPOMI overpasses near each site.
citation: Cite the individual TCCON site DOI listed at tccondata.org for each station used.

name: NOAA ObsPack (GLOBALVIEWplus)
summary: Curated collection of surface, tower, aircraft and ship greenhouse-gas measurements prepared for model evaluation and inversions.
spatial: Point and profile measurements at many sites
provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory and contributing labs
access: Free; request form on the ObsPack portal, and contact data contributors before use
limitations: Sparse in tropics and Southern Hemisphere
Mole fractions at the surface, not columns
bestFor: Evaluating model fields and constraining inversions with in situ data.
useWith: Combine with satellite columns in inversions; compare with CarbonTracker or CAMS.
citation: Cite the ObsPack product DOI for the release used, plus any contributing lab requested in its data policy.

name: Surface Ocean CO2 Atlas (SOCAT)
summary: Quality-controlled surface ocean fCO2 measurements (about 44 million observations) from ships, moorings and drifters, with gridded products.
temporal: Individual measurements; daily and monthly gridded
strengths: Standard dataset for ocean carbon sink estimates
limitations: Uneven sampling in space and time
bestFor: Ocean CO2 flux estimates and ocean prior fluxes.
useWith: Pairs with MiCASA, ODIAC and GFED to complete a global flux budget.
citation: Bakker, D. C. E. et al., Surface Ocean CO2 Atlas (SOCAT), Earth System Science Data (use the version cited).

name: GEDI L4B Gridded Aboveground Biomass Density
summary: Lidar-based gridded estimates of aboveground biomass density, a proxy for carbon stored in forests.
provider: NASA / University of Maryland / ORNL DAAC
bestFor: Forest carbon stock mapping and biomass baselines.
useWith: Use stocks with MiCASA fluxes and GFED fire emissions to study land carbon change.
citation: Dubayah, R. et al., GEDI L4B Gridded Aboveground Biomass Density, Version 2.1, ORNL DAAC (verify).
